page: Amazon Web Services r6id.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores using dedicated allocation and symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation is sized at 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Local storage is provided through 1900 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are included.

Benchmark results place general compute and memory throughput consistently in the middle 50% tier. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 14050.0 and a single-core score of 1634.0, paired with a multi-core stress-ng metric of 30966.98. The memory subsystem recorded 142.07 GB/sec for large block read-only bandwidth and 67.57 GB/sec for large block writes. In-memory and transactional testing showed 31.0 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and a PassMark database score of 14858.19. Static web serving throughput reached 35.34 GB/sec.

The CPU includes AVX-512 vector and encryption instructions, achieving 29107.3 points in PassMark CPU encryption. For machine learning tasks, the CPU executes lightweight model inference adequately, reaching 232.33 tokens/sec generation on a small 135M model and 17.93 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. However, performance decreases severely for large language models, generating only 2.26 tokens/sec on a 70B model, placing it in the bottom 10% and highlighting the absence of dedicated accelerators.

With its generous 256 GB RAM footprint paired with 1900 GB of fast local NVMe storage, the r6id.8xlarge balances compute density with high-speed caching and scratch space. This makes it technically suited for in-memory databases like Redis, transactional relational database management systems requiring fast local tempdb or WAL storage, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL pipelines.
